name: Jason
description: Brother of Onias the high priest; bought the high priesthood from Antiochus Epiphanes and brought Jerusalem to Greek fashions, building a place of exercise and training youth after the heathen manner; undermined in turn by Menelaus and driven out, he later attacked the city, slew his own countrymen, and died in exile after being driven from land to land

points: After the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus called Epiphanes took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest. This is his own blood brother. Not only does Onias have to deal with Simon of the tribe of Benjamin; his own blood brother is trying to take the priesthood from him. Put yourself in his sandals: his good friend Simon turned on him, and now his brother.

This is one of the origins of these black fraternities. After the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus Epiphanes took the kingdom, “Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest.” The high priesthood was up for bid. In the law you had to come through Aaron’s line to be high priest, but when the Greeks took over, they bid for it with money.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: All of this causes us to love the glory of the other nations more than ourselves, and you see the same thing in history. “But after the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus, called Epiphanes, took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest”. This was the Greek captivity: he went underhand to his oppressors to become ruler over the people.

Such was the height of Greek fashions, an increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch and no high priest. Sports is a Greek fashion: the coliseums are shaped the same way as the football stadiums today, and in them we were the entertainment.

When he had gotten the rule into his hand, he forthwith brought his own nation to the Greekish fashion; he put down the governments which were according to the law and brought up new customs against the law; he built gladly a place of exercise, brought the chief young men under his subjection, and made them wear a hat: the hat of Hermes, shown in class alongside the discus statue. Such was the height of Greek fashions and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest. Though he had the rule, the writer says he is not the true high priest.

The side effect of having no racial identity, of worshipping a god who does not look like you, is that you hate your people and your race and love everybody else. “Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest”: when the Greeks came into Jerusalem they brought Greek fashions among our people, the same as today.

“Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest.” This is the history Christians don’t know about and don’t understand.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: “Through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest”. Jason was the high priest who bought his way in; he didn’t even earn it. No high priest for real. Pam is our people; T.D. Jakes, these guys are our people. But they will sell their people down the river for a paycheck to stay in the good graces of massa. You gain the whole world and lose your own soul by lying to them.

note.label: 2819 CHURCH & THE ACCESS PORTAL TO HELL

points: Then Jason, who had undermined his own brother, being undermined by another, was compelled to flee into the country of the Ammonites. Now the high priest is of the tribe of Benjamin. You cannot make this stuff up.

When there was gone forth a false rumour, as though Antiochus had been dead, Jason took at the least a thousand men and suddenly made an assault upon the city, and Menelaus fled into the castle. Now Menelaus is running from his one-time friend Jason, whose priesthood he took. But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen, because he despised his own people.

“But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, not considering that to get the day of them of his own nation would be a most unhappy day for him; but thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen, whom he conquered.” Jason in the Bible hated his own countrymen, and Jason Whitlock, with the same name, is the same: he accused our bishop of being a racial idolater while he is a financial idolater, loving master with all his heart and soul, like all the rest of those men.
